body.purpose: Everything: labels, values, table cells, prose.

shadows.name: functional-card

shadows.name: overlay
shadows.purpose: Toasts only. The one element that floats over the page rather than sitting in it.

shadows.name: focus-halo
shadows.purpose: The primary focus affordance on inputs and buttons. The border shift alone is too quiet to rely on.

motion.name: state-transition
motion.purpose: Colour, background, border and box-shadow on every interactive element. The system has exactly one timing.

components.name: Primary Button

components.description: The neutral peers of a primary action — section tabs, month arrows, Today. Hover floods the outline with its own colour and flips the text to white.

components.name: Small Destructive Button
components.description: How every removing action is drawn — Deregister, Remove, Detach. Destructive actions are never filled, and in a table row they are always btn-sm.

narrative.overview:
This is a practical printed document that a family keeps to hand — a handbook the federation printed and the unit filled in. It is not trying to be distinctive. It is trying to be legible, familiar, and recognisably the federation's, so that a parent who has never seen this particular software still knows how to read it: every page opens the same way, every action is a button in the place buttons go, and nothing on screen is competing with the thing they came to do.

Structurally the system is two layers that never mix. A vendored theme — Les Scouts' own template-unite, a Bootstrap build carrying the federation's graphical charter — supplies every shape, colour and typeface. On top sits a single small override file, static/css/troopconnect.css, holding only the deviations: a hero band, a first-run wizard, an agenda grid, one table column with a ceiling. The rule that makes this work is that the override file stays small; a rule that merely restates one the theme already makes is a liability, because the theme can move under it and the local copy would win.

The result is deliberately unglamorous and consistently so. Density follows the task rather than the brand: a settings page is a stack of cards, a member list is a striped table, a form is one labelled field per block. The federation shows up in flat charter colour, in bold Muli, and in one ornamental gesture — the flag silhouette repeated behind a banner — and nowhere else. There is no troop-level colour, no theme picker, no second accent: the palette is the federation's, and the unit's identity is carried by its name and the logo it uploads.
keyCharacteristics: Bootstrap's own primitives, used as intended, restyled only where a task needs it
One typeface (Muli) and one flat charter palette, both inherited, neither configurable
A sky-blue banner with the federation flag behind it as the recurring page opener
Thin 1px lines and soft 0.25rem corners; depth by border, not by shadow
Paper-filled fields on a paper-coloured page, separated by a border and a blue focus halo
Two shells: the site (fixed 110px navbar) and the first-run wizard (its own page, same theme)

rules.name: The Federation's Ink Rule
rules.body: The palette belongs to Les Scouts and a troop never configures it. A troop owns its name, its logo, its favicon, its branches and its content — it does not own colour. A "match my logo" or theme-picker feature is a departure from this system, not a refinement of it.

rules.name: The Charter-Only Rule
rules.body: A new state gets a colour from this list or it gets no colour. Charter hues may carry meaning only through an explicit mapping — today that is the agenda's three activity types (charter-blue-deep reunion, charter-green-deep day, charter-plum weekend) — and never by inventing a hue or reaching for a Bootstrap default that the theme did not override.

rules.name: The One Voice Rule
rules.body: The application sets Muli and only Muli. The theme's Housepaint (a hand-painted face), CaveatBrush, Mali-Bold and Roboto Mono are available in the stylesheet and appear nowhere in the product; reaching for one is a departure from the incumbent system, not a flourish within it.

rules.name: The Weight-Not-Colour Rule
rules.body: Emphasis is 700, not a hue. Never colour text to make it louder — the palette has no text colours to spend, and every heading already shares the body's ink.

rules.name: The Border-or-Shadow Rule
rules.body: Never both on the same surface. If a card needs a shadow, its border goes; if it needs a border, it gets no shadow. The two are the same signal, and using them together makes a surface look like two.

rules.name: The Flat-Page Rule
rules.body: The page itself is flat. No section, band or container lifts off the background — depth is spent only on cards that behave as separate units, and never as decoration.

rules.name: The Two-Scale Rule
rules.body: A new block sizes itself from the override scale and never from an ad-hoc value; a page's structure keeps to the theme's Bootstrap ramp. Bootstrap caps h1 at 2.5rem above 1200px, so the desk's 3rem question stays the largest type on the page at every width. Adding a step to either scale without recording it here is how a system stops being one.

rules.name: The Never-On-The-Field Rule
rules.body: Copy is never set on a charter field. White type fails AA on the Baladins blue and dark type fails on the other three, so the paper goes between them every time. The field may carry meaning; it may not carry words.

dos: Do load the vendored theme first and troopconnect.css second — the order is what makes the override layer work, and reversing it silently disables every deviation.
Do keep troopconnect.css small. Only put a rule there that the theme does not already state; a restated rule is a copy that can win after a theme upgrade.
Do pair a .btn-primary with .btn-outline-primary on the same row, and give a destructive action an outline button — Deregister, Remove and Detach are all outline, never filled.
Do give every field a <label class="form-label" for="...">, then the control, then .form-text for help — in that order.
Do use role="alert" on errors and role="status" on confirmations, and keep errors as text under the control rather than as a red field.
Do wrap every .table in .table-responsive, and put a max-width on a free-text cell instead of letting the row grow.
Do open every members page with the banner (hat_title + hat_text).
Do ship a plain href or action alongside every HTMX attribute, so the page still works when the swap does not.
Do set the navbar's 110px height in px and keep --site-navbar-height in px to match; the navbar does not scale with the root font size.
Do put copy on a sheet of paper over a charter field, never on the field itself.
donts: Don't edit anything under app/static/vendor/template-unite/. It is byte-identical to a known upstream commit, and a local edit is lost at the next theme refresh and invisible in the diff that would have caught it.
Don't introduce a colour. The palette is the federation's — if a new state needs a colour it takes one from the list above or it takes none.
Don't set Housepaint, CaveatBrush, Mali or Roboto Mono. The application speaks Muli; those faces exist in the theme for pages this project does not build.
Don't put a border and a shadow on the same card — that is two signals for one surface.
Don't colour body or heading text to add emphasis. Weight is the tool.
Don't style the site header with a bare header selector. The homepage editor exports content that can carry its own <header>, and a bare selector reaches into authored content.
Don't use window.alert() for feedback. Toasts and inline alerts exist, and a browser alert cannot be translated or styled.
Don't build a second modal. #modal / #dialog is the dialog, and every HTMX view targets it.
Don't add a page that has to be read on hover to be understood — nothing in this system depends on pointer state to be legible.
